blocks.text: Aramaic buṭmā, from which Arabic buṭm is borrowed, Fraenkel 139. The single occurrence of buṭnīm in the Targum is a learned conjecture. Talmudic buṭmā Rh. 23^{a}. Bb. 80^{b}. jKil. I 27^{a}. Targ. Jes. 1, 30. 6, 13 (TW. אלה [ʾlh]). 1 S. 17, 2. 2 S. 18, 9. Hos. 4, 13. Onkelos and jGn. 35, 4. The Samaritan has דחלתה [dḥlth] (דהלאה [dhlʾh]), and has thus misunderstood the word and thought of ʾelōᵃh.
bōṭem, which BJ. cites from Asaph's boṭmīm, is not Hebrew: it has been retained from the Syriac source. Ph. Hasade 6, 206.

Syriac: ܒܛܡܬܐ [beṭmtā] in the Bible translation for ʾēlā, ʾēlōn, ʾallā, ʾallōn, boṭnīm, lōṭ (rōtem). a) τερέβινθος [terebinthos], b) τέρμινθος [terminthos], c) κῶνος [kōnos]? — Neo-Syriac: bīṭmā, bīṭemtā, a terebinth-tree.

a) BB. 274. 790. 829_{18} (corrupted here). b) Gal.-Üb. c) ? ܐܩܘܢܘܣ [ʾqwnws] ܩܘܢܘܣ [qwnws] BB. 277_{10}. Arabic among the Syrians. d) بطم [buṭm] BB. 274. 277. e) الحبّة الخضراء [al-ḥabba al-khaḍrāʾ] BA. 2354. BB. 381 Honein. 829 corrupt. ܩܘܠܘܦܘܢܝܘܣ [qwlwpwnyws] 1796 (= kolophonia)*). 1934: الحبّة الخضراء الاكبر [al-ḥabba al-khaḍrāʾ al-akbar] ܒܛܡܐ ܪܒܬܐ [beṭmā rabbtā]. — Τερεβινθίνη [Terebinthinē] (ῥητίνη [rhētinē]) Gal.-Üb. 240. List 99. Sachau Inedita 95. BB. 790. f) ܕܘܥܬܐ ܕܒܛܡܬܐ [dūʿtā d-beṭmtā] [Duval-Berth. 2, 45]. BB. 801 corrupt. 790 = 180. g) القاوازا [al-qāwāzā] = h) علك النباط [ʿilk al-nabāṭ]**) [ἀλκυόνιον [alkyonion]? Is there perhaps a confusion of ܪܘܥܬܐ [rwʿtʾ] BB. 179 and ܕܘܥܬܐ [dūʿtā]?] Perhaps علك البطم [ʿilk al-buṭm]? Card. j) φρυκτὴ ῥητίνη [phryktē rhētinē]***) resina terebinthi PSm. 325 ܪܘܛܝܢܐ [rwṭynʾ]. Sergius calls f) ܢܛܡܬܐ [nṭmtʾ] BB. 404. 546. 789 f. 801. 1796.

The resin of the terebinth, buṭm, Musil 3, 230. Nuwairī (E. Wiedem. XLIX 19). ^{1}) ʿilk el-buṭm, resin of the حبّة الخضراء [ḥabbat al-khaḍrāʾ], comes from the Maghreb, Palestine, Syria and neighboring regions. As distinct from this, pistachio resin is called ^{2}) ʿilk el-anbāṭ,†) but mastic ^{3}) ʿilk al-rūmī. Kašef Sha 1393 ff. has ^{1}) and ^{3}) likewise, but ^{2}) without translation, and ^{4}) ʿilk šaǵar ul-fustuḳ: gum of the pistachio tree.

Arabic: buṭm (ZDPV. 27, 25. 30, 134. Robinson I 346. III 221). Ascherson, Sitzungsberichte der naturforsch. Freunde 1882 21. II. Nr. 2, p. 13: beṭūm, in Algiers the Tripolitanian terebinth, probably P. atlantica Desf. It is a loanword (Fraenkel 139). The

Jacob of Edessa: from the trees of Gilead; from beṭmē; from ܥܠܟܐ [ʿelkā] Nöld. OS. 577.
Kroner Maim. passim. קלפוניא [qlpwnyʾ] for terebinth oil in Maimonides' ink recipe, Peēr hadōr Nr. 45 f. 14. GA. Maim. Nr. 53, Salm. Hyl. 170 ff.
